findings: Several recent production issues were caused by malformed internal links containing undefined path segments or legacy organization routes.
There was no dedicated QA script to catch these patterns before deployment.
actions_taken: Added a route link quality scanner that fails on hardcoded undefined route segments and warns on legacy organization route patterns.
Added npm script quality:routes for Codex and CI usage.

Promote route quality scan into security:ci after false positives are resolved.

findings: Billing plan IDs drifted between public catalog/signup/add-ons and backend entitlements/checkout: public catalog used starter/growth while backend canonical plans are essential/professional/business/enterprise.
The public billing catalog used Stripe environment keys that do not match .env.example and the server checkout plan mapping.

A direct corrective patch to billing/Stripe-adjacent code was blocked by connector safety controls, so the patch was prepared for manual Codex/local application instead of being forced through GitHub API.
actions_taken: Prepared a safe alignment patch: canonicalize public plan IDs to essential/professional/business/enterprise, keep starter/growth aliases for old links, align Stripe env key names, and prevent Enterprise from being treated as self-serve checkout until explicitly enabled.
Recorded the blocked application attempt and next manual application steps.
next_cycle_focus: Apply the prepared billing plan alignment patch locally with Codex or a human review because it touches checkout and Stripe-adjacent code.
After applying, run npm run typecheck and npm run security:ci.
Verify /pricing, /signup?plan=professional, /signup?plan=growth legacy alias, and /dashboard/organizations/add-ons?plan=enterprise do not unlock entitlements without checkout/webhook confirmation.
